messages:
customer_acme_app: Hey support — we rotated our API key this morning and now all requests from our background worker are failing with 401 invalid_api_key. No code changes except secret update in k8s.

maya_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the curl you used (sanitized) and confirm whether you're using a hosted or dedicated deployment? Also please include any x-redwood-request-id from response headers if present.

customer_acme_app: Here's the curl I'm using (redacted):
```bash
curl -v -H 'X-Api-Key: REPLACED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response is HTTP/1.1 401 and body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}. No x-redwood-request-id header in the response. We're on hosted (default) account.

jordan_infra: Quick guess — looks like you're sending X-Api-Key which some older helpers accepted, but the platform expects Authorization: Bearer <KEY> for hosted endpoints. Also confirm the env var name in your k8s manifest. If you have both REDWOOD_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY set, the process might pick the wrong one (shadowing).

customer_acme_app: Hmm we used a helper that sets REDWOOD_KEY in the pod spec, and also our Helm chart had a legacy value REDWOOD_API_KEY from CI. I checked the secret file and it had a trailing newline (secret created from literal file). I trimmed the newline and restarted the pod, still 401.

maya_support: Two things to check: 1) header format (Authorization: Bearer <key>) and 2) whether the key you rotated is a Dedicated key. Dedicated keys are scoped to a private hostname and won't auth against the hosted public API — that will return a 401 without request-id sometimes. Can you paste the key id prefix (just the id prefix, not the secret) from the dashboard (e.g., kd_ vs hk_).

servicebot: Key metadata for kd_8f3a...: scope=[generate,embeddings], deployment=dedicated-acme-east, expires=2026-05-01.

customer_acme_app: Oh — the new key we generated is labeled kd_8f3a... I assumed all keys work against the same endpoint. We had a Dedicated trial set up and I mistakenly created a Dedicated key. So that explains it.

maya_support: That explains the 401. Fix options: 
- Use the dedicated endpoint/hostname tied to that key (your dedicated host should be listed in the dashboard under Private/Dedicated) OR
- Create a hosted API key (hk_...) for requests to https://api.redwood.inference .
If you want, I can temporarily create a short-lived hosted key you can test with while you reconfigure.

customer_acme_app: Switching the worker to the dedicated hostname fixed it. Worker now authenticates and requests succeed. Thanks! :thumbsup:

maya_support: Great — marking this resolved. Notes for internal: common pattern = key-type mismatch (dedicated vs hosted) + env var shadowing + header format. Recommend doc snippet addition for quick diagnosis and a k8s secret example showing REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_KEY.
